subject: Discovery recap & next steps - Acme Enterprise
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps - Acme Enterprise

Hi Sam -

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. I captured the items we discussed and highlighted the bits that will matter to procurement.

TL;DR - Acme is evaluating a hosted inference solution to reduce per-token costs and improve latency for your customer-facing summarization feature. You're targeting a pilot starting in June with an evaluation that must demonstrate <100ms median latency on 512-token tails and a 25-30% reduction in inference cost per 1k tokens versus current setup.

Pain points / current state
- Current stack: in-house PyTorch model served on cloud VMs via a custom API gateway; no GPU pooling or KV caching; frequent cold-start latency spikes.
- Cost pressure: token costs and operational overhead are high; team expects measurable unit-economics improvement.
- Reliability: production incidents during peak traffic; need better graceful degradation and fallback.

Success criteria for pilot (what would make this a go/no-go)
- Latency: median end-to-end 95-99th percentile meeting targets (<100ms median on sample workload).
- Cost: 20-30% reduction in per-token cost after batching/caching optimizations.
- Integration: client-facing API parity with minimal dev lift (SDK or lightweight adapter).
- Observability: per-route latency & cost dashboards + tracing hooks for SRE.

Decision process & timeline (as discussed)
- Pilot decision maker: Sam (PM) + Engineering lead (Lisa) and procurement looped for legal/terms.
- Procurement involvement: will be needed for contract terms, SSO/KMS, and DPA.
- Timeline: pilot kickoff target - June 1; procurement review in late May.

Initial commercial guardrails (for procurement framing)
- Pilot options: Hosted API pay-as-you-go (fast, minimal commitment) OR 3-month reserved capacity for predictable throughput.
- Indicative commitment for pilot: $20k-60k TCV depending on traffic profile and whether you choose reserved capacity.
- Discounting: standard pilot discounts apply for evaluation; precise numbers once we have traffic profile and SLA requirements.

Next steps
1) Can you confirm the procurement contact (name + email) who will lead the contract/IT security review?
2) We'll follow up with a short SOW template and an indicative pricing range tailored to the traffic profile you shared.
3) Rafael (cc'd) will prepare a short POC plan and requirements doc for the engineering sync.

Attachments: redwood-platform-one-pager.pdf (overview)

If that all looks right, propose a 30-min procurement + engineering sync week of May 25-29.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Sam - looping Lisa + procurement as requested. Quick responses to the pricing ask and logistics so you have something to share with finance: 

Indicative commercial guardrails (high level, subject to traffic profile)
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): typical pilot spend range for customers with your traffic profile: $15k-40k/month. This is easiest to spin up (no infra commit) and includes token-level reporting & standard SLAs.
- Dedicated / reserved capacity (3-month commitment): typical TCV: $45k-120k for a 3-month block depending on peak concurrency needs. Reserved capacity gives cost predictability and lower per-token unit cost at high throughput.
- Add-ons of note: extended observability retention and enterprise support are additional fees we can outline.

Procurement / security items we can prepare ahead of your review
- SOC 2 Type II report, DPA template, KMS integration notes (support for AWS KMS/HSM).
- Standard SOW template and pilot statement-of-work (attached).

Next logistical steps
1) Rafael will draft a short POC plan with required test vectors and acceptance criteria; he'll share that by next Wed (Mar 24).
2) I can share a redlined SOW template and an indicative pricing worksheet once you confirm whether you prefer Hosted API vs Reserved capacity for the pilot.
3) Proposed procurement + engineering sync: May 26, 10:00-10:45am PT - happy to adjust.

Attachments: acme-sow-template.docx
